newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks steady, trade to remain slow.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks steady, trade to remain slow.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly steady on lower turnover on Friday and market participants expected trade to slow down during the year-end festivities.

"Investors have confidence only in two top stocks (Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva)," said Marijana Reskovac from Karlovacka Banka, adding they would account for most of the next week's activity.
She said buyers' interest had waned and sellers were no longer in a hurry to get rid of their stocks, forcing many brokerages to close shop.
Two of six active issues rose, two fell and two were flat. Volume halved at 2,577 shares, turnover also lower at 3.2 million kuna.
Total weekly turnover was also lower at 17.5 million kuna due to a two-day bourse closure.

Top gainer and most actively traded Zagrebacka Banka rose 10 kuna to 1,080, with 1,949 shares sold. Its GDRs trading on Seaq International rose steadily this week to edge down to $20.56 on Friday from $20.78 before Christmas.
Other fully-listed stock, drugs firm Pliva, closed flat at 14,000 kuna after testing a lower 13,800 level. It sold 70 shares.
Pliva's GDRs fell to $53.5 on Friday from Monday's record high of $54 on the London Stock Exchange.
Traders suspected they would not encourage a boom on the Zagreb bourse before well into next spring.
The only other gainer confectioner Kras inched up one kuna to 420, with 60 units traded.
Bigger of the two decliners, hotelier Laguna, lost 50 kuna on volume of 36 units in a first deal from a fortnight ago. Food processor Podravka edged down two kuna to 213 on volume of 384 shares.
Hotelier Jadranturist traded flat at 205 kuna, selling 78 shares.
